## Method

Seven fresh browser contexts per workload, alternating client order. Both clients use memory persistence, identified-only person profiles, the same 250-button document, and the same event properties. After 50 warm-up captures, the timed loop captures 500 events. The benchmark asserts that every event reaches the client’s before-send callback. PostHog’s bot filter is disabled for the automated browser, and its rate limit is raised to avoid measuring dropped events.

Bundles use esbuild, ES2022, ESM, minification, and tree-shaking. Gzip bytes include every JavaScript body requested by the page, including PostHog’s dynamically loaded assets and configuration. Event-only and browser comparisons use PostHog’s no-external entry point. The slim comparison uses module.slim.no-external.js; diagnostics use the standard package entry and locally served npm assets. Surveys are explicitly disabled. No requests reach PostHog.

Times are medians. Startup script CPU is Chromium’s ScriptDuration after initialization and the same settling interval for each client. Capture time measures synchronous foreground work, not later serialization, compression, network delivery, or backend processing. The test does not measure long-session memory use, mobile battery cost, or cloud playback. Raw samples and loaded script paths are in output/comparison.json.

## Scope and quality

MiniHog implements fewer APIs and browser compatibility branches than posthog-js. It targets ES2022 browsers and explicit feature imports; PostHog’s SDK supports a broader product surface, browser compatibility, targeting, and integrations. Matching feature categories here does not imply identical event properties or heuristics. These measurements support size and performance claims for these workloads, not a universal claim that one library has better quality.

MiniHog’s release checks enforce 95% statement, branch, function, and line coverage per package; lint and types; packed-package validation; clean npm and pnpm consumers; and removal of every unused optional entry point. Browser tests exercise masked recording, diagnostics, deferred startup, consent, and navigation. Cloud ingestion and playback require separate integration verification.

## Reproduce

Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`, then `pnpm benchmark`. Use `pnpm comparison:update` to regenerate this document. The comparison version is pinned in the workspace lockfile; results vary by browser, machine, application, and feature selection.

Implementation: [comparison script](scripts/compare-posthog.mts). API boundaries: [core documentation](packages/core/README.md). PostHog reference: [JavaScript SDK documentation](https://posthog.com/docs/libraries/js).
